A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this project is a first step in the direction of building an affective, multimodal, and multiparty tutoring dialogue platform, that is based on an analysis of a human-human tutoring corpus, and a dialogue platform that allows the tutor (robot) to maintain a well coordinated and balanced conversation, and to measure incrementally attention and dominance of the participants, in an effort to maximize the agreement, the contribution to solve a task, and the engagement.

we have built a novel human-robot interaction experimental setup, collected a human-human dialogue dataset, and built a situated model of a multiparty dialogue, and designed a dialogue system platform that allows us to build a robot that can engage in a multiparty tutoring dialogue.

the dialogue system can be used to build an affective, human-like tutor that is able to maintain a well-coordinated, balanced and engaging conversation, with two participants, that attempts to maximise the agreement and the contributions to solve the task, and that can be used for educational and team building applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a multimodal, situated dialogue system can be a powerful tool to build robots capable to maintain engaging, and well coordinated multiparty spoken interactions, and that can be used in collaborative learning, tutoring, and team building applications.

a robot can be a valuable partner in a multiparty interaction, and it can be designed to be a tutor, that is capable of coordinating the interaction between the participants, and to help them solve a task, while maintaining a well balanced and engaging interaction.

the design of a human-like, multimodal dialogue system that is capable of regulating and coordinating multiparty spoken interactions can be used to design and build more engaging and effective robots for collaborative tutoring and educational applications.
